title: NIR-to-NIR emission on a water-soluble {Er6} and {Er3Yb3} nanosized molecular wheel

synthesis.procedure: Following the previously reported Ln6 procedure, Er(NO3)3·6H2O (0.6 mmol) was dissolved in MeOH/CH2Cl2 (5 mL:15 mL), then triethanolamine (1.2 mmol) and triethylamine (4.8 mmol) were added. The clear pink solution was stirred for four hours, during which a small amount of precipitate formed. The mixture was filtered and the filtrate layered with Et2O. Pink crystals of [Er6(teaH)6(NO3)6] appeared after two days. The main text only cites the prior procedure and does not give amounts. Unit-cell parameters matched the earlier Er6 structure (literature CCDC 1876163); no new CCDC deposition for {Er6} is reported in this paper.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction, filtration, and Et2O layering
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered and layered with Et2O; pink crystals formed after two days

properties.summary: Aqueous {Er6} shows NIR-to-NIR emission: excitation at 980 nm gives a band centred near 1530 nm (4I13/2 → 4I15/2), still visible when the laser power is lowered from 200 to 20 mW. Emission is stronger in D2O than in H2O; a 5 mg mL−1 D2O solution saturated the detector (limit 65000 counts), so 2.5 mg mL−1 was used. Intensity falls exponentially as the H2O fraction increases. Solid-state diffuse reflectance shows the Er 4I11/2 ← 4I15/2 absorption near 980 nm (10204 cm−1), weaker than the ~379 nm 4G11/2 band.

measurements.name: emission maximum
measurements.conditions: aqueous solution, 5 mg mL−1, excitation 980 nm, laser power 20–200 mW; 4I13/2 → 4I15/2 (Fig. 2a)

measurements.name: detector saturation limit
measurements.conditions: {Er6} in D2O at 5 mg mL−1, excitation 980 nm

synthesis.procedure: The {Er6} procedure was followed using Yb(NO3)3·6H2O (0.6 mmol) instead of the erbium salt, with triethanolamine (1.2 mmol) and triethylamine (4.8 mmol) in MeOH/CH2Cl2 (5 mL:15 mL), stirring for four hours, filtration, and layering with Et2O. The isolated product is an unsymmetrical [Yb6(teaH)6(NO3)5(H2O)](NO3)·(CH2Cl2)2(MeOH)2 wheel rather than the symmetric [Ln6(teaH)6(NO3)6] analogue; one Yb(III) is seven-coordinate and the others are eight-coordinate. Crystallographic empirical formula C40H86N12O39Yb6Cl4 (CCDC 1958096, RUMVON).
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction, filtration, and Et2O layering
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered and layered with Et2O under the same conditions as {Er6}

synthesis.procedure: The same MeOH/CH2Cl2 procedure was followed using Er(NO3)3·6H2O (0.3 mmol) and Yb(NO3)3·6H2O (0.3 mmol), triethanolamine (1.2 mmol), and triethylamine (4.8 mmol). The mixture was stirred for four hours, filtered, and layered with Et2O. ICP-OES metal ratio: calculated Er 50% / Yb 50%; found Er 44% / Yb 56%. Crystallographic empirical formula reported as C43H121N12O43Er3Yb3 (CCDC 1958091, RUMVIH); the structure is a merohedral twin.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction, filtration, and Et2O layering
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered and layered with Et2O; crystalline product isolated

properties.summary: Isostructural {Er3Yb3} is a water-soluble NIR-to-NIR emitter. Under the same 5 mg mL−1 aqueous conditions and 980 nm excitation used for {Er6}, the ~1530 nm Er emission intensity increases by about 15%, attributed to the larger Yb absorption cross-section at 980 nm, Yb-to-Er energy transfer, and reduced Er concentration quenching. Diffuse reflectance shows a much stronger and broader absorption near 980 nm (10204 cm−1), assigned to Er 4I11/2 ← 4I15/2 and Yb 2F5/2 ← 2F7/2.

measurements.name: relative emission intensity increase
measurements.conditions: aqueous solution, 5 mg mL−1, excitation 980 nm, compared with {Er6} under the same conditions (Fig. 2d)

measurements.conditions: aqueous emission, 5 mg mL−1, variable laser power

measurements.name: absorption band
measurements.conditions: diffuse reflectance near 980 nm; Er 4I11/2 ← 4I15/2 and Yb 2F5/2 ← 2F7/2 (SI Table S2, Fig. S7)

synthesis.procedure: The same procedure used for {Er6} was followed with Y(NO3)3·6H2O (0.6 mmol), triethanolamine (1.2 mmol), and triethylamine (4.8 mmol) in MeOH/CH2Cl2 (5 mL:15 mL), stirring for four hours, filtration, and Et2O layering. {Y6} was prepared as a diamagnetic analogue for D2O NMR water-stability studies; no separate crystal structure or CCDC entry is given.

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered and layered with Et2O under the same conditions as {Er6}
